description: Establish a trustworthy baseline before changing the layout schema, and record the facts every later feature is measured against. Three things must be true before FEAT-002 starts: the environment is green so fidelity numbers are comparable to the committed ones, the uncommitted working-tree state of both repos is written down (this plan builds on it rather than reverting it), and the per-report distillation facts and backend coverage are computed rather than assumed. This feature also repairs one thing found during planning: the committed Chromium render of secondary/school-results has been overwritten in the working tree by a WeasyPrint render, and that artifact is the demonstrable-fidelity sample shipped in the sdist. No source code changes here.
steps: cd /root/apis/mussannoni && uv sync. Then `make doctor` and record the output verbatim. The goal is 'environment ready: measurements are comparable to the committed results'. If pdftoppm, agent-browser or any licensed face is missing, record exactly what is missing and its impact - the raster metrics from tools/compare.py will then not be comparable to committed report.json values. Do NOT relax anything to compensate. NOTE FOR ANY RE-RUN: this host is Ubuntu and scripts/setup-environment.sh is dnf/rpm-based, so `make setup` does not apply; see findings for how the dependencies were satisfied.

Record the baseline test and lint state: `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pytest`, capturing pass/skip counts. The previously recorded state from task-pluggable-engine-and-pdf-size was 664 passed / 46 skipped; confirm or correct that against the current working tree, which has uncommitted changes to table.py and package_resources.py.

Record `make check-resources` result. Because tools/package_resources.py and four layout.json are modified in the working tree, state clearly whether the committed resources currently match what the modified distiller produces. If they do not, regenerate with `make package-resources` FIRST so the baseline is self-consistent, and record that you did.

Write down the full uncommitted state of both repos: `git -C /root/apis/mussannoni status --short` and `git -C /root/apis/mussannoni diff --stat`, and `git -C /root/apis/backend-sis status --short -- app/services/exametrics/mussannoni/ app/api/exametrics/v1/mussannoni.py`. Confirm the characterisation in context.json: that the package_resources.py diff both fixed the compound-page grid selection and introduced the band loss, and that the backend's pre-package engine is deleted-but-uncommitted.

Restore the clobbered evidence artifact: `git -C /root/apis/mussannoni checkout -- output/secondary/school-results/rendered.pdf` and delete the untracked output/secondary/school-results/render-meta.json. Verify the restored file is 2,570,884 bytes, opens with pymupdf, and has 15 pages. Record why: every calibration in this repo was measured against Chromium, and task-pluggable-engine-and-pdf-size/FEAT-002 findings state that WeasyPrint fidelity is a separate, ungated question.

Compute and record the per-report distillation table for ALL 46 reports with /root/apis/mussannoni/.venv/bin/python, reading templates/*/*/fixture.json and src/mussannoni/resources/*/*/layout.json. Per report: level, report_key, page-1 column count, modal/body column count, whether the first page is compound, label-row index, how many page-1 rows _transplanted_header discards, whether layout body is null, distilled rows_per_page, the reference's own page-1 row count and fullest-page row count, and whether table.y_pt + header.height_pt + rows_per_page * body.row_height_pt exceeds page.height_pt. Confirm or correct the three known compound reports and their 5 / 13 / 2 dropped rows, and report how many of the 46 currently overflow their page box.
Record which reports carry decorations.loose_lines or decorations.vectors, and which have layout body == null (the table API cannot drive those at all, independently of everything else in this task).

Compute and record the backend coverage table for ALL 46 reports with /root/apis/backend-sis/venv/bin/python3, importing mussannoni, app.services.exametrics.mussannoni.bindings.binding_for, ...headers.unsafe_header_reason, ...resolve.has_row_source and ...service.binding_matches_layout. Per report print ordinal, level, key, scope, binding column count vs layout label count, match, unsafe reason, row source, and the resulting blocker; then group the blockers by cause and state how many reports generate today. Do NOT touch the database and do NOT query information_schema.

Record the current generated output for secondary/school_results as the before-state: render it in-process through the package with a synthetic 44-row payload, write to /tmp, and record page count, per-page candidate row counts, and the page-1 extracted text. This is the artifact FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 must visibly improve. Clean up /tmp afterwards.

Confirm whether the package the backend imports is the working tree or an installed copy: /root/apis/backend-sis/venv/bin/python3 -c "import mussannoni, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(mussannoni.__file__).resolve(), mussannoni.__version__)". Record it, because it determines whether backend verification in FEAT-006/FEAT-007 sees package edits.
acceptance_criteria: `make doctor` output is recorded, and any missing binary or font is documented with its impact on metrics.
`uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pytest` baseline results are recorded, and `make check-resources` is recorded as clean (regenerating first if needed, and saying so).
The uncommitted state of both repos is written into findings, including confirmation that the package_resources.py diff introduced the band loss while fixing the grid selection.
output/secondary/school-results/rendered.pdf is restored to the committed 2,570,884-byte 15-page Chromium render and the stray render-meta.json is gone.
A 46-row distillation table is recorded, confirming exactly which reports are compound, how many rows each loses, and how many reports overflow their measured page box.
A 46-row backend coverage table is recorded with blockers grouped by cause and a count of reports that generate today.
The before-state render of secondary/school_results is recorded (page count, rows per page, page-1 text) and no scratch files remain outside /tmp.
No source file in either repo is modified by this feature.

findings.host: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, apt-based. This matters: scripts/setup-environment.sh is written for dnf/rpm and CANNOT run here, which is the whole reason `make doctor` reported everything missing. The script was never broken - it was written for the Amazon Linux 2023 sandbox recorded in the two earlier tasks' context.json. No change was made to the script; the dependencies were satisfied the Ubuntu way instead.

environment_fixed.licensed_faces: RESOLVED, all 7 now [ok]. ttf-mscorefonts-installer 3.8.1ubuntu1 was ALREADY installed and had already placed the faces at /usr/share/fonts/truetype/msttcorefonts/ under the exact lowercase names tools/fonts.py::SYSTEM_FONTS expects (arial.ttf, arialbd.ttf, ariali.ttf, arialbi.ttf, times.ttf, timesbd.ttf, timesi.ttf - themselves relative symlinks to the Capitalised real files). Only the PATH differed: SYSTEM_FONTS hardcodes /usr/share/fonts/msttcore/. Created that directory with 7 symlinks and ran fc-cache -f. Verified genuine metrics load through the chain with pymupdf.Font(fontfile=...): Arial ascender 0.9053 / descender -0.2119, Times ascender 0.8911 / descender -0.2163. No font data was copied or redistributed.
environment_fixed.pdftoppm: already present, poppler 24.02.0 (committed baselines were measured against 24.08.0 - a rasteriser minor-version difference, recorded here because raster metrics are compared at 300 dpi).
environment_fixed.doctor: `make doctor` now prints 'environment ready: measurements are comparable to the committed results' with pdftoppm [ok], chromium [ok], weasyprint [ok] and all 7 licensed faces [ok].

environment_blocked.chromium_engine: NOT usable on this host, and this is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Installed agent-browser via npm (npm prefix is /root/.npm-global, which is not on PATH, so it was symlinked to /usr/local/bin/agent-browser; version 0.27.0). `doctor` then reports chromium [ok] because it only tests that the binary is on PATH. The binary does not work: every render fails with 'Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11) (after 5 retries - daemon may be busy or unresponsive)' and then a 30s timeout on `close`. agent-browser is a client/daemon tool and the daemon cannot run in this container. `agent-browser doctor` itself exits 2 with no output. Three separate attempts failed identically, so this was diagnosed rather than retried further.
environment_blocked.root_cause_and_the_available_alternative: Snap Chromium 152.0.7977.82 IS installed at /snap/bin/chromium and /usr/bin/chromium-browser, and driving it DIRECTLY works: `chromium-browser --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-dev-shm-usage --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf-no-header --print-to-pdf=<path> <html>` reported '11184 bytes written' and produced a valid 1-page PDF. That is exactly the invocation in the DELETED backend module, recoverable with `git -C /root/apis/backend-sis show HEAD:app/services/exametrics/mussannoni/pdf.py`. That module also documented the trap this host has, and the trap was reproduced and confirmed here: with a work directory under /tmp the snap build fails with 'Failed to write file /tmp/...: No such file or directory' because it gets a private /tmp, while the same command with a work directory outside /tmp succeeds. src/mussannoni/document.py::render_html_to_pdf renders inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, i.e. /tmp, so a direct-Chromium engine must place its work outside /tmp. DECISION REQUIRED FROM THE USER before acting - adding an engine to src/mussannoni/engines.py is a public API addition beyond this task's agreed scope, so it is not being done unilaterally.
environment_blocked.consequence_for_the_task: tests/test_engine.py::test_optimization_shrinks_pdf_while_preserving_pixels renders through the chromium engine and therefore FAILS here. FEAT-008's acceptance criterion 'pytest green' cannot be met on this host until the chromium engine question is settled. Nothing else in the suite depends on it.

baseline.ruff: uv run ruff check . -> All checks passed!
baseline.pytest: uv run pytest -> 1 failed, 722 passed, 46 skipped in 507s. The single failure is the chromium-engine test above. NOTE the earlier tasks recorded 664 passed / 46 skipped; the suite has grown to 723 collected since, so 722 passed is the correct new baseline, not a regression.
baseline.check_resources: `make check-resources` -> 'package resources are current'. The committed src/mussannoni/resources/ already matches what the MODIFIED tools/package_resources.py produces, so the baseline is self-consistent and no pre-emptive regeneration was needed.

findings.evidence_artifact_restored: output/secondary/school-results/rendered.pdf had been overwritten in the working tree by a WeasyPrint render (756,932 bytes, and an untracked render-meta.json recording {"engine": "weasyprint", "optimized": true}). Restored with `git checkout --` and the stray sidecar deleted; verified 2,570,884 bytes / 15 pages / 792x612. This matters because every calibration in the repo was measured against Chromium, task-pluggable-engine-and-pdf-size/FEAT-002 findings state plainly that WeasyPrint fidelity is a separate ungated question, and this file is the sample pair the sdist ships to make the fidelity claim demonstrable.

distillation_table_46_reports.compound_first_page: 3 reports, confirming the planning figures exactly: secondary/school-results (page1 11 cols vs body 9, label row 6, 5 rows dropped), primary/school-results (25 vs 23, label row 14, 13 rows dropped), primary/region-ufaulu-masomo (28 vs 20, label row 3, 2 rows dropped).
distillation_table_46_reports.body_null: ZERO reports have body == null. The table API can drive all 46, so there is no report excluded from this task on that ground.
distillation_table_46_reports.page_box_overflow: 7 reports currently declare a rows_per_page whose page-1 table would exceed the measured page box - FIVE MORE THAN THE PLAN ASSUMED. secondary/school-results +49.37pt, secondary/council-schools-rank-subjectwise +26.74, secondary/subject-schools-rank +26.48, primary/school-results +20.5, secondary/region-mobility +18.67, secondary/region-schools-rank-overall +13.76, secondary/region-schools-rank-government +4.53. FEAT-003 is therefore materially wider than 'fix secondary/school-results' and its acceptance criteria must name all 7.
distillation_table_46_reports.capacity_disagreement: rows_per_page disagrees with the reference's own fullest-page row count in 38 of 46 reports, in BOTH directions - it overstates (primary/council-best-students 28 vs 24, secondary/region-top-schools 13 vs 11) and understates (primary/council-school-rank-ufaulu-alama 53 vs 63, secondary/region-schools-rank-government 77 vs 80). Overstating overflows the page; understating wastes pages. Only 8 reports agree. CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-23: the per-report 'reference fullest-page row count' used here was computed by subtracting a label row from each continuation page, which is wrong wherever continuation pages carry no label band - it understated secondary/school-results as 36 where the true count is 39, and that report's rows_per_page of 39 is in fact correct. The direction and corpus-wide scale of the disagreement stand, but FEAT-003 must RE-MEASURE the per-report reference counts with per-page label-band detection before treating any number here as a target. This confirms the deleted TemplateSpec's insistence that capacity is measured, not computed, and makes FEAT-003 a corpus-wide correction rather than a corner case.
distillation_table_46_reports.decorations: loose_lines on 8 reports (primary/region-halmashauri-jumla 4, primary/region-halmashauri-masomo 4, primary/region-ufaulu-masomo 4, primary/school-results 1, secondary/council-schools-rank-subjectwise 4, secondary/council-subjects-rank 5, secondary/region-subjects-performance 4, secondary/subject-schools-rank 4). vectors on 7 reports (primary/council-ufaulu-wa-masomo 1, primary/region-shule-bora-jumla 2, primary/region-shule-bora-masomo-jumla 2, primary/region-shule-bora-masomo-serikali 2, primary/region-ufaulu-masomo-jumla 1, secondary/council-schools-rank-subjectwise 1, secondary/subject-schools-rank 1). Both sets must survive FEAT-002's page-1 rework.

backend_coverage_46_reports.blockers_by_cause: 6 x NO BINDING + NO ROW SOURCE (primary council_top_schools_kimasomo_overall, council_top_schools_kimasomo_serikali, council_subject_summary, council_ufaulu_wa_masomo, region_shule_bora_masomo_serikali, region_shule_bora_masomo_jumla); 3 x NO ROW SOURCE (secondary council_best_students_subjectwise, council_schools_rank_subjectwise, region_mobility); 1 x COUNT 10!=11 + NO ROW SOURCE (secondary region_best_students_subjectwise); 1 x COUNT 37!=38 (secondary region_council_performance); 1 x COUNT 22!=23 (primary school_results); 1 x COUNT 29!=30 + UNSAFE HEADER (primary council_kata_rank_alama); 1 x UNSAFE HEADER (primary council_school_rank_ufaulu_alama); 1 x COUNT 28!=20 (primary region_ufaulu_masomo). resolve.ROW_QUERIES has 34 entries.
backend_coverage_46_reports.key_reading_of_that_table: The COUNT and UNSAFE HEADER blockers are largely CONSEQUENCES OF THE DISTILLATION DEFECTS, not backend mistakes. primary/school_results (22 vs 23) and primary/region_ufaulu_masomo (28 vs 20) are precisely the two compound primary reports - region_ufaulu_masomo's binding of 28 matches the reference's page-1 grid while the distilled layout reports the 20-column body grid, so the binding is right and the layout is the odd one out. Both UNSAFE HEADER reports are headers.py's 'header band holds more than one band of measured figures' verdict, which is what a flattened multi-band page looks like from the outside. So FEAT-002 through FEAT-004 should unblock roughly 4 reports and must be re-measured against this table afterwards. The genuinely missing work is the 6 unbound primary reports and the 4 without a row source - those are backend data-coverage gaps, not package defects, and FEAT-008 must report them as such rather than claiming them.
backend_coverage_46_reports.constraint_respected: Computed entirely by importing modules in the backend venv. No database query, no information_schema, no HTTP.

findings.before_state_secondary_school_results: Rendered in-process with a synthetic 44-row payload BEFORE any change: 2 pages, 33,862 bytes; page 1 carried 35 candidate rows and page 2 carried 9, rather than the intended 39 + 5, because the declared capacity does not fit. Page-1 extracted text runs 'S0333 - MWANZA SECONDARY SCHOOL' then 'DIVISION PERFORMANCE SUMMARY' then straight to 'CNO' - the heading with no table beneath it, which is the user-visible symptom that opened this task. The reference puts 26 candidate rows on page 1 and 39 on its fullest continuation page. CORRECTED 2026-09-23: this finding originally said '36 on continuation pages', which was measured from page 2 (not the fullest page: 37 rows against 39 on pages 3-13) and with a label row subtracted that continuation pages do not carry. The consequence is that rows_per_page=39 is CORRECT for this report's continuation pages and the defect is confined to page 1.
findings.package_import_path: /root/apis/backend-sis/venv/bin/python3 resolves mussannoni to the INSTALLED copy, not the working tree, so FEAT-006 and FEAT-007 must reinstall the package before backend verification can see package edits. Recorded here so that is not discovered late.
findings.no_source_changes: This chore changed no source file in either repository. The only repository changes are the restored output/secondary/school-results/rendered.pdf, the deleted stray render-meta.json, and this .agents/tasks/task-layout-band-fidelity/ plan directory. System-level changes outside the repos: /usr/share/fonts/msttcore/ symlinks, fc-cache refresh, the global agent-browser npm package and its /usr/local/bin symlink.
findings.capacity_root_cause_measured: Added 2026-09-23 from reading tools/package_resources.py::_rows_per_page and distil_layout against the fixtures. TWO independent faults, both corpus-wide. (a) HEIGHT DIVISION: capacity is `tallest summed band height // modal row height`, so a total band or wrapped row taller than modal counts as more than one row and inflates the number - the 'overstates' direction. (b) PAGE-1 HEADER_ROWS APPLIED TO EVERY PAGE: distil_layout computes body_skip once from page 1 and _rows_per_page slices page['rows'][body_skip:] on every body page, but a fixture's per-page header_rows on a CONTINUATION page marks a data row, not a label band - verified on secondary/school-results, whose pages 2-13 declare header_rows=1 while page 2 row 0 is candidate S0333-0027 - so real data rows are discarded and capacity is understated. 40 of 46 reports are multi-page and only 11 continuation pages across the corpus declare header_rows=0, so this affects most of it. The compound branch already sets body_skip=0 and is correct on this point, which is why secondary/school-results' continuation capacity of 39 is right. (c) Deriving capacity from available area is wrong too: (612 - 54.24) // 12.72 = 43 against the reference's 39. (d) Page 1's true front band measures 168.20pt (rows 0-6) against the distilled header's 111.05pt, the 57.15pt difference being the dropped summary band, so page-1 capacity must be computed against the restored band from FEAT-002, not the truncated header.
